description:
Remove the sidebar's Google S2 favicon fallback that can transmit tab, bookmark, and history domains (`components/sidebar.js:64-77,324-329`). Reuse Chrome's packaged `/_favicon/` endpoint pattern from `components/BookmarksButton.js` and provide an in-package fallback without third-party network disclosure.

Add or update repository privacy documentation so tabs, bookmarks, history, screenshots/thumbnails, sync storage, and any remaining network behavior are accurately described. Include a Chrome Web Store disclosure checklist; do not claim compliance that was not verified outside the repository.

Acceptance criteria:
- No `google.com/s2/favicons` request remains in shipped code.
- Missing favicons degrade to a packaged/local fallback.
- Privacy documentation matches actual extension behavior.
- Tests or reproducible validation cover tabs, bookmarks, history, missing favicons, and failure fallback.

Implemented the favicon privacy fix and repository disclosures.

- Replaced the sidebar's Google S2 fallback in both shipped trees with a shared Chrome `/_favicon/` helper.
- Routed sidebar tabs, bookmark/history rows, and search result favicon construction through the packaged endpoint.
- Added a generated letter-tile fallback for missing URLs and failed favicon loads, with no third-party fallback request.
- Added `PRIVACY.md` covering tabs, bookmarks, history, locally extracted page metadata, screenshots/thumbnails, local and sync storage, custom backgrounds, permissions, remaining network behavior, retention, and an explicitly unverified Chrome Web Store disclosure checklist.
- Linked the privacy policy from the README.
- Added regression tests for tab, bookmark, and history favicon URLs, missing favicons, failed loads, and both shipped sidebar copies.

Validation:

- `node --test`: 21/21 passing.
- Repository-wide literal scan: no `google.com/s2/favicons` reference.
- `git diff --check`: passing.
- Root and `meridian-extension` copies of all affected shipped files are byte-identical.
Reviewer approved: implementation/output verified against the task scope; combined suite passes (41/41) and shipped source/package parity passes.
